title: Keeping girls in secondary school
summary: A project works in a rural district where girls leave secondary school earlier than boys. It tackles four reasons together: cost, unsafe journeys, expectations at home, and how quickly schools respond when a girl starts missing class.
whyThisWorks: The problem statement says who is affected, how much and why, without naming the project. Each activity answers one of the stated reasons. Outputs are things the project team delivers and can count directly. Outcomes are changes in attendance and behaviour that it influences but doesn't control. The assumptions name what else must hold true, such as schools having enough places for larger classes.

items: In a rural district, 38% of girls leave before finishing lower secondary, compared with 21% of boys. Main reasons: cost, unsafe journeys and household work.
assumptions: School records show the gap between girls and boys reliably

indicators.text: Share of girls enrolled in Year 7 who are still enrolled in Year 9
indicators.target: Tracked for context. Targets are set at outcome and impact level.

items: Bursaries for fees, uniforms and materials for 300 at-risk girls
Walking groups and bicycle loans for girls living 3 km+ away
Monthly family groups with chiefs and religious leaders
Train 40 teachers to spot early signs of drop-out
assumptions: Bursary funding arrives before each term

indicators.text: Number of girls whose bursary is paid before the start of term

items: 300 girls a year get full bursaries before term
Safe-travel schemes on 6 routes, for up to 150 girls
Family groups in 10 villages, reaching 400 parents
40 teachers trained and using an early-warning checklist
assumptions: Families take up bursaries without stigma

indicators.text: Number of trained teachers returning the early-warning checklist each month
indicators.target: 35 of 40 by the end of year 1

items: Cost no longer the main reason girls stay home
Teachers act early when attendance drops
assumptions: No sharp rise in other household costs, such as food

indicators.text: Average attendance rate of girls in participating schools
indicators.meansOfVerification: School attendance registers, checked each term

items: More girls move from Year 7 to Year 9
Families plan for daughters to finish lower secondary
assumptions: Enough school places and teachers for larger classes
Pressure for early marriage doesn't increase

indicators.text: Share of girls enrolled in Year 7 who are still enrolled in Year 9
indicators.meansOfVerification: School enrolment records, checked yearly with the district education office

items: Girls finish lower secondary at the same rate as boys

indicators.text: Gap between girls' and boys' lower-secondary completion rates

draftPairs.weak: Improved attendance of girls thanks to bursaries
draftPairs.improved: 300 girls a year get full bursaries before term
draftPairs.why: Better attendance is a change in behaviour, so it belongs under outcomes. An output is something the project delivers and can count directly.

draftPairs.improved: Girls finish lower secondary at the same rate as boys
draftPairs.why: The first version is too broad to measure or to link back to the activities. The improved version names one specific change that can be observed.
